body_md:
# Audit programme: Revenue and trade receivables

*Area: CYC-REV — Revenue and receivables | Illustrative programme (not a firm methodology) | 2026-10-23*

## 1. Engagement context and assumptions

Revenue is a presumed fraud-risk area: recognition depends on when the entity's performance criteria are met, and pressure to meet targets concentrates risk at the period end. Trade receivables carry valuation risk through expected credit losses and existence risk where billing is divorced from delivery. Side agreements, bill-and-hold and channel stuffing are the classic concealment routes.

Assumptions: the programme is adapted to the entity's size, systems, assessed risks and materiality. It does not replace professional judgement or the engagement partner's direction.

## 2. Objective

Obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that revenue and trade receivables are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.

## 3. Relevant financial statement areas

- CYC-REV: Revenue and receivables

## 4. Relevant assertions

- [BAL-COM] Completeness
- [BAL-EXI] Existence
- [BAL-VAL] Accuracy, valuation and allocation
- [DIS-COM] Completeness
- [TRN-ACC] Accuracy
- [TRN-CLS] Classification
- [TRN-COM] Completeness
- [TRN-CUT] Cut-off
- [TRN-OCC] Occurrence

## 5. Potential risks

- [R-BNK-002] **Overstated interest income on non-performing loans** — Interest accrued on doubtful loans may never be collected; without suspension or adequate provision against the accrued interest, income and receivables are ove...
- [R-FRD-003] **Fictitious or premature revenue to meet targets** — Revenue is recorded for transactions that did not occur, or genuine revenue is recognised before the applicable recognition criteria are satisfied, in order to ...
- [R-REV-001] **Revenue overstatement through premature recognition** — Revenue may be recorded before the entity has satisfied the recognition criteria, so reported revenue and the related trade receivable are overstated for the pe...
- [R-REV-002] **Revenue understatement through cut-off errors (late recording)** — Sales earned before the reporting date may be omitted from the current period, understating revenue and trade receivables. The factor makes this possible; it do...
- [R-REV-003] **Fictitious or unsupported sales recorded in the ledger** — Sales may be recorded that have no underlying economic event - fictitious invoices, or genuine invoices without the dispatch or performance that would make them...
- [R-REV-004] **Deliberate manipulation of revenue to achieve incentive targets** — Where incentives depend on revenue targets, there is a fraud risk that revenue is deliberately misstated - pulled forward, deferred, inflated or fabricated - to...
- [R-REV-005] **Material misstatement through unusual or non-routine year-end transactions** — Unusual transactions recorded near year-end may lack commercial substance, be recorded in the wrong period, or be structured to achieve a desired accounting out...
- [R-RTL-001] **Unrecorded sales and theft of takings (shrinkage)** — Cash sales may be skimmed before recording, voids and refunds may be fictitious, and shrinkage may go unrecorded - understating revenue and overstating the resu...
- [R-RTL-002] **Premature or overstated recognition of supplier rebates** — Rebate income may be recognised before the qualifying purchase volumes are achieved, or accrued on terms the supplier has not agreed - overstating income and re...
- [R-RTL-003] **Understated deferred revenue from unredeemed gift cards and loyalty points** — Liabilities for unredeemed cards and points may be released prematurely, or breakage recognised aggressively - understating deferred revenue and overstating cur...
- [R-TEL-002] **Incorrect allocation of consideration across bundle components and premature revenue recognition** — Consideration may be allocated using unsupported stand-alone selling prices, or recognised before the related service is delivered, accelerating revenue into ea...
- [R-TEL-003] **Systematic billing errors from rating or tariff configuration** — A misconfigured tariff, discount or rating rule is applied to every affected transaction until detected, producing systematic over- or under-billing across the ...

## 6. Relevant controls

- [C-BNK-002-1] Prevent accrual of uncollectible interest.
- [C-FRD-002] Detect fraud and override by giving staff a safe route to report concerns.
- [C-FRD-005] Prevent premature or fictitious revenue recognition driven by target pressure.
- [C-REV-001] Prevent revenue being recorded before recognition criteria are met.
- [C-REV-002] Detect premature revenue recognition around the period end.
- [C-REV-003] Detect sales earned but not recorded at the reporting date.
- [C-REV-004] Ensure sales are recorded in the correct accounting period.
- [C-REV-005] Prevent sales being recorded without evidence of dispatch or performance.
- [C-REV-006] Detect unsupported sales promptly.
- [C-REV-007] Provide independent oversight of revenue susceptible to manipulation.
- [C-REV-008] Prevent unauthorised or unsupported manual adjustments to revenue.
- [C-REV-009] Ensure unusual transactions have genuine commercial substance before they are recorded.
- [C-REV-010] Detect year-end transactions recorded without substance or in the wrong period.
- [C-RTL-001-1] Detect missing takings promptly.
- [C-RTL-001-2] Prevent fictitious voids/refunds as a skimming method.
- [C-RTL-002-1] Ensure income is recognised only on agreed terms.
- [C-RTL-003-1] Ensure the liability is complete and breakage is authorised.
- [C-TEL-002-1] Prevent unsupported allocation keys entering the billing system.
- [C-TEL-002-2] Ensure allocation is applied consistently to all contracts.
- [C-TEL-003-1] Detect unrated or misrated usage before billing.
- [C-TEL-003-2] Prevent defective rating logic reaching production.

## 7. Preliminary planning considerations

Understand each material revenue stream: contract terms, when recognition criteria are met, and how billing links to dispatch/acceptance evidence. Map the order-to-cash process and identify where management could override it. Assess period-end concentration and related-party sales. For receivables: understand the ECL model, its inputs and segmentation, and the history of collection. Set confirmation strategy early — confirmations must be controlled by the auditor, not the client.

## 8. Suggested tests of controls

- [P-REV-004] Reperform the billing-to-dispatch matching control

## 9. Suggested substantive analytical procedures

- [AP-REV-101] Monthly revenue trend vs prior year and budget
- [AP-REV-102] Gross margin by product line vs prior periods
- [AP-REV-103] Revenue vs non-financial data (units dispatched)
- [AP-REV-201] Receivables days vs credit terms trend
- [AP-REV-202] Ageing profile vs prior year
- [AP-REV-203] Bad-debt provision vs write-off history

## 10. Suggested tests of details

- [P-REV-001] Vouch recorded sales to evidence that recognition criteria were met
- [P-REV-002] Inspect contracts and terms for selected revenue transactions
- [P-REV-003] Test revenue cut-off around the reporting date
- [P-REV-005] Trace pre-year-end dispatch notes to the sales ledger
- [P-REV-006] Test post-year-end sales for pre-year-end dispatch
- [P-REV-007] Inspect the period-end dispatch-to-invoice reconciliation
- [P-REV-008] Vouch sales invoices to dispatch and order evidence
- [P-REV-009] Analyse revenue against dispatch volumes and trends
- [P-REV-010] Confirm selected sales and balances directly with customers
- [P-REV-011] Analyse revenue performance against incentive targets
- [P-REV-012] Inspect manual journal entries affecting revenue near period end
- [P-REV-013] Discuss incentive schemes and revenue pressures with management and those charged with governance
- [P-REV-014] Inspect large and unusual year-end transactions
- [P-REV-015] Vouch unusual transactions to independent third-party evidence
- [P-REV-016] Scan revenue and journal listings for unusual items

## 11. Sampling considerations

Vouching: stratified or haphazard samples weighted to period-end and unusual items. Receivables confirmations: monetary-unit or stratified sampling with coverage of material balances; all non-responses get alternative procedures. Cut-off: examine ALL material items in the cut-off window — sampling is not appropriate for cut-off assertions.

## 12. Evidence to obtain

- [E-REV-001] Sales invoices and billing reports
- [E-REV-002] Dispatch notes, delivery records and customer acceptance
- [E-REV-003] Sales contracts, orders and terms of sale
- [E-REV-004] Goods dispatch register around year-end
- [E-REV-005] Sales daybook and ledger extracts
- [E-REV-006] Period-end cut-off reconciliation and accrual schedules
- [E-REV-007] Sales invoices selected for vouching
- [E-REV-008] Dispatch and delivery evidence for sampled sales
- [E-REV-009] Customer confirmations and correspondence
- [E-REV-010] Incentive and bonus plan documents
- [E-REV-011] Manual journal entries affecting revenue
- [E-REV-012] Board minutes and performance reports
- [E-REV-013] Manual journal entries and supporting schedules for unusual transactions
- [E-REV-014] Contracts and agreements for unusual transactions
- [E-REV-015] Counterparty correspondence and documented management explanations

## 13. Expected documentation

For each procedure: objective, procedure performed, population and sample basis, evidence obtained (with references), results, exceptions and their resolution, and a conclusion linked to the assertion. Preparer and reviewer sign-off with dates. Cross-reference working papers so a reviewer can reperform the work.

## 14. Evaluation of exceptions

Cut-off errors: quantify, determine whether isolated or systematic, extend the window. Confirmation differences: investigate each; request client follow-up then perform alternative procedures (subsequent cash, dispatch records). ECL model challenges: stress key assumptions and compare with subsequent collection experience.

## 15. Possible further procedures

Where exceptions indicate a systematic issue: extend the procedure, perform alternative procedures, involve specialists (valuers, tax, IT), or escalate to the engagement manager. Document the reasoning for the chosen response — procedure count alone proves nothing.

## 16. Completion considerations

Analytical review of revenue trends and margins by stream; subsequent-receipts testing for receivables; confirm all material exceptions are resolved or accumulated as misstatements.

## 17. Conclusion requirements

Conclude per assertion whether sufficient appropriate evidence was obtained. Unresolved exceptions are accumulated as misstatements and evaluated for materiality, individually and in aggregate. The conclusion must stand without the programme — a reviewer should reach the same conclusion from the working papers alone.

## 18. Relevant source references

- [ISA-240]
- [ISA-500]
- [ISA-501]
- [ISA-505]
- [ISA-520]
- [ISA-540R]
- [ISA-560]
- Companies Act, 2017 ss.246–253 (auditor provisions) [KR-CA2017-246 … KR-CA2017-253]

body_md:
# Audit programme: Inventory

*Area: CYC-INV — Inventory | Illustrative programme (not a firm methodology) | 2026-10-23*

## 1. Engagement context and assumptions

Inventory is high-risk for existence (theft, fictitious stock) and valuation (obsolescence, net realisable value below cost). The auditor generally attends the physical count; where attendance is impracticable, alternative procedures are required and the limitation is documented.

Assumptions: the programme is adapted to the entity's size, systems, assessed risks and materiality. It does not replace professional judgement or the engagement partner's direction.

## 2. Objective

Obtain sufficient appropriate evidence over the existence, ownership and valuation of inventory at the reporting date.

## 3. Relevant financial statement areas

- CYC-INV: Inventory

## 4. Relevant assertions

- [BAL-COM] Completeness
- [BAL-EXI] Existence
- [BAL-VAL] Accuracy, valuation and allocation
- [TRN-ACC] Accuracy

## 5. Potential risks

- [R-INV-001] **Inventory loss through theft, unauthorised removal or unrecorded damage** — Inventory may be stolen, lost or removed without authorisation, or damaged without the loss being recorded. If such losses are not identified and recorded, inve...
- [R-MFG-001] **Misallocated overheads and misstated work in progress** — Overhead rates may be based on outdated budgets, normal capacity may be overstated (absorbing abnormal idle costs), or allocation bases may not reflect actual c...
- [R-MFG-002] **Variances buried rather than analysed, misstating inventory and cost of sales** — Material variances may indicate that standards are outdated (misstating inventory) or that real inefficiencies, waste or price changes are being hidden in cost ...

## 6. Relevant controls

- [C-INV-001] Prevent unauthorised removal of inventory.
- [C-INV-002] Detect unrecorded inventory losses and ensure records agree with physical quantities.
- [C-MFG-001-1] Keep absorption rates current and capacity assumptions realistic.
- [C-MFG-001-2] Prevent capitalisation of abnormal production costs.
- [C-MFG-002-1] Ensure variances are understood and standards stay current.

## 7. Preliminary planning considerations

Understand storage locations, count instructions, and segregation between counters and record-keepers. Assess count date vs year-end (roll-forward/back needed). Identify slow-moving, specialised or third-party-held stock. Review costing method and overhead absorption policy for manufactured inventory.

## 8. Suggested tests of controls

- *(No tests of controls in the library for this area yet.)*

## 9. Suggested substantive analytical procedures

- [AP-INV-301] Inventory days by category vs prior year
- [AP-INV-302] Inventory growth vs revenue growth (overstocking signal)
- [AP-INV-303] Slow-moving ratio vs obsolescence provision

## 10. Suggested tests of details

- [P-INV-001] Reconcile the inventory listing to the general ledger
- [P-INV-002] Attend the physical inventory count and inspect selected items
- [P-INV-003] Perform two-directional test counts
- [P-INV-004] Investigate material differences between physical counts and inventory records
- [P-INV-005] Inspect inventory movement records around the count date
- [P-INV-006] Review adjustment journals relating to shortages and losses
- [P-INV-007] Inspect warehouse access records and investigate unusual movements
- [P-INV-008] Evaluate whether discrepancies require accounting adjustments or additional procedures

## 11. Sampling considerations

Test counts: select from floor-to-records and records-to-floor, weighted to high-value lines. Price testing: sample purchases and NRV calculations. 100% examination of high-value or judgemental items.

## 12. Evidence to obtain

- [E-INV-001] Inventory listing (detailed inventory records)
- [E-INV-002] General ledger reconciliation
- [E-INV-003] Physical count sheets
- [E-INV-004] Auditor test-count records
- [E-INV-005] Inventory movement reports (goods received / dispatch notes)
- [E-INV-006] Adjustment journals for shortages and losses
- [E-INV-007] Warehouse access records
- [E-INV-008] Explanations and supporting documents for discrepancies

## 13. Expected documentation

For each procedure: objective, procedure performed, population and sample basis, evidence obtained (with references), results, exceptions and their resolution, and a conclusion linked to the assertion. Preparer and reviewer sign-off with dates. Cross-reference working papers so a reviewer can reperform the work.

## 14. Evaluation of exceptions

Count differences: investigate, assess whether the count as a whole can be relied on. NRV below cost: require write-down. Obsolete stock without provision: quantify and accumulate.

## 15. Possible further procedures

Where exceptions indicate a systematic issue: extend the procedure, perform alternative procedures, involve specialists (valuers, tax, IT), or escalate to the engagement manager. Document the reasoning for the chosen response — procedure count alone proves nothing.

## 16. Completion considerations

Analytical procedures on inventory days and margins; subsequent-sales review for NRV; roll-forward/back working papers agreed to the count.

## 17. Conclusion requirements

Conclude per assertion whether sufficient appropriate evidence was obtained. Unresolved exceptions are accumulated as misstatements and evaluated for materiality, individually and in aggregate. The conclusion must stand without the programme — a reviewer should reach the same conclusion from the working papers alone.

## 18. Relevant source references

- [ISA-500]
- [ISA-501]
- [ISA-520]
- Companies Act, 2017 ss.246–253 (auditor provisions) [KR-CA2017-246 … KR-CA2017-253]

# Audit programme: Cash and bank balances

*Area: CYC-CSH — Cash and bank | Illustrative programme (not a firm methodology) | 2026-10-23*

## 1. Engagement context and assumptions

Cash is highly susceptible to misappropriation; bank balances turn on reconciliations whose long-outstanding items can conceal errors or fraud. Dormant, suspense and foreign-currency accounts are easily overlooked.

Assumptions: the programme is adapted to the entity's size, systems, assessed risks and materiality. It does not replace professional judgement or the engagement partner's direction.

## 2. Objective

Obtain sufficient appropriate evidence over the existence and completeness of cash and bank balances and the reliability of reconciliations.

## 3. Relevant financial statement areas

- CYC-CSH: Cash and bank

## 4. Relevant assertions

- [BAL-COM] Completeness
- [BAL-EXI] Existence
- [BAL-VAL] Accuracy, valuation and allocation
- [TRN-CLS] Classification
- [TRN-CUT] Cut-off
- [TRN-OCC] Occurrence

## 5. Potential risks

- [R-CSH-001] **Errors and irregularities in bank transactions remain undetected** — Unrecorded bank charges, direct debits, errors, or misappropriation through the bank account are not identified because the reconciliation is not subject to ind...
- [R-CSH-002] **Unauthorised or fraudulent payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries** — Funds are disbursed to fictitious or improper beneficiaries, whether through falsified supporting documents, diverted supplier payments, or payments with no bus...
- [R-CSH-003] **Cash misstated through year-end transfer cut-off errors** — Transfers recorded as received before year-end but not yet dispatched (or vice versa) double-count or omit cash, overstating or understating the reported balanc...
- [R-CSH-004] **Cash on hand misappropriated or misstated** — Physical cash is removed or lost without detection, and the recorded balance exceeds cash actually held....

## 6. Relevant controls

- [C-CSH-001] Ensure bank errors and irregularities are detected and investigated promptly.
- [C-CSH-002] Prevent stale items from permanently distorting the reported cash balance.
- [C-CSH-003] Prevent payments to fictitious or improper beneficiaries.
- [C-CSH-004] Ensure only genuine, properly supported payments are released.
- [C-CSH-005] Ensure inter-account transfers are completely and accurately recorded on both sides.
- [C-CSH-006] Prevent cut-off errors and window dressing through year-end transfers.
- [C-CSH-007] Detect shortages or misappropriation of cash on hand.
- [C-CSH-008] Prevent unauthorised removal of physical cash.

## 7. Preliminary planning considerations

List ALL bank accounts including closed and dormant ones — obtain bank confirmations for every account, controlled by the auditor. Identify who prepares vs reviews reconciliations (segregation). Note foreign-currency translation policy.

## 8. Suggested tests of controls

- [P-CSH-001] Inspect bank reconciliations for independent review
- [P-CSH-008] Test payment authorisation controls
- [P-CSH-014] Observe the entity's cash count procedures

## 9. Suggested substantive analytical procedures

- [AP-CSH-701] Interest income vs average cash balances
- [AP-CSH-702] Cash vs working-capital trend
- [AP-CSH-703] Large and round-amount transfer scan

## 10. Suggested tests of details

- [P-CSH-002] Reperform the year-end bank reconciliation
- [P-CSH-003] Vouch aged outstanding items to subsequent clearance
- [P-CSH-004] Obtain direct bank confirmation of balances
- [P-CSH-005] Vouch unusual payments to supporting documentation
- [P-CSH-006] Analyse payments by beneficiary for anomalies
- [P-CSH-007] Trace new beneficiaries to verification evidence
- [P-CSH-009] Match both sides of year-end transfers
- [P-CSH-010] Inspect transfer advices and bank statements
- [P-CSH-011] Reperform the in-transit reconciliation
- [P-CSH-012] Count cash on hand
- [P-CSH-013] Reconcile the count to cash records and investigate differences

## 11. Sampling considerations

Reperform 100% of material bank reconciliations — sampling is not appropriate. Investigate ALL long-outstanding reconciling items, not a sample.

## 12. Evidence to obtain

- [E-CSH-001] Bank reconciliation
- [E-CSH-002] Bank statement
- [E-CSH-003] Bank confirmation letter
- [E-CSH-004] Outstanding items schedule
- [E-CSH-005] Payment register / bank payment listing
- [E-CSH-006] Supporting documents for payments
- [E-CSH-007] Beneficiary verification records
- [E-CSH-008] Inter-account transfer register
- [E-CSH-009] Bank transfer advices
- [E-CSH-010] Cash count sheets
- [E-CSH-011] Petty cash records and vouchers
- [E-CSH-012] Auditor's cash count record

## 13. Expected documentation

For each procedure: objective, procedure performed, population and sample basis, evidence obtained (with references), results, exceptions and their resolution, and a conclusion linked to the assertion. Preparer and reviewer sign-off with dates. Cross-reference working papers so a reviewer can reperform the work.

## 14. Evaluation of exceptions

Stale outstanding cheques/deposits: investigate, consider write-back. Unrecorded bank charges or direct debits: accumulate. Confirmation differences: resolve with the bank.

## 15. Possible further procedures

Where exceptions indicate a systematic issue: extend the procedure, perform alternative procedures, involve specialists (valuers, tax, IT), or escalate to the engagement manager. Document the reasoning for the chosen response — procedure count alone proves nothing.

## 16. Completion considerations

Subsequent bank statements reviewed for clearance of outstanding items; confirmations reconciled to the trial balance.

## 17. Conclusion requirements

Conclude per assertion whether sufficient appropriate evidence was obtained. Unresolved exceptions are accumulated as misstatements and evaluated for materiality, individually and in aggregate. The conclusion must stand without the programme — a reviewer should reach the same conclusion from the working papers alone.

## 18. Relevant source references

- [ISA-500]
- [ISA-505]
- Companies Act, 2017 ss.246–253 (auditor provisions) [KR-CA2017-246 … KR-CA2017-253]

body_md:
# Audit programme: Purchases and trade payables

*Area: CYC-PUR — Purchases and payables | Illustrative programme (not a firm methodology) | 2026-10-23*

## 1. Engagement context and assumptions

The primary risk is completeness — unrecorded liabilities and expenses, especially accruals at the period end. Cut-off errors shift costs between periods. Supplier statement reconciliations are the key independent check.

Assumptions: the programme is adapted to the entity's size, systems, assessed risks and materiality. It does not replace professional judgement or the engagement partner's direction.

## 2. Objective

Obtain sufficient appropriate evidence over the completeness, occurrence and cut-off of purchases and the completeness and valuation of trade payables.

## 3. Relevant financial statement areas

- CYC-PUR: Purchases and payables

## 4. Relevant assertions

- [BAL-COM] Completeness
- [BAL-EXI] Existence
- [TRN-ACC] Accuracy
- [TRN-COM] Completeness
- [TRN-CUT] Cut-off
- [TRN-OCC] Occurrence

## 5. Potential risks

- [R-PUR-001] **Invalid purchases recorded and paid for goods not received** — Purchases may be recorded - and paid - for goods or services never received. This is a potential misstatement and a possible control deficiency; the factor does...
- [R-PUR-002] **Unrecorded liabilities and understated purchases at the reporting date** — Goods received before year-end but invoiced afterward may be omitted from purchases and payables, understating liabilities. The factor describes a cut-off expos...
- [R-PUR-003] **Payments to fictitious or altered suppliers; invalid payable balances** — Uncontrolled changes to supplier master data may divert payments to fictitious suppliers or altered bank accounts, and may create invalid payable balances. The ...
- [R-PUR-004] **Duplicate recording of purchases and duplicate payments** — The same supplier invoice may be recorded twice, overstating purchases and payables, and may be paid twice, causing a cash loss. Duplication is usually error, b...
- [R-PUR-005] **Cut-off misstatement of purchases and trade payables** — Purchases recorded in the wrong period misstate both purchases and payables at the reporting date. Cut-off errors can fall in either direction and are often err...

## 6. Relevant controls

- [C-PUR-001] Prevent payment for goods not received.
- [C-PUR-002] Detect invoices paid without evidence of receipt.
- [C-PUR-003] Ensure liabilities for goods received are recorded at the reporting date.
- [C-PUR-004] Record purchases in the correct accounting period.
- [C-PUR-005] Prevent unauthorised or fictitious suppliers entering the payment process.
- [C-PUR-006] Detect fictitious or inappropriate suppliers in the master data.
- [C-PUR-007] Prevent the same invoice being recorded twice.
- [C-PUR-008] Prevent paid invoices re-entering the payment process.
- [C-PUR-009] Ensure purchases are recorded in the correct period.
- [C-PUR-010] Detect cut-off errors in purchases after the reporting date.

## 7. Preliminary planning considerations

Understand the procure-to-pay process: GRN/invoice/PO matching, who can post journals to payables, and the accruals process. Obtain supplier statements for major suppliers early. Plan after-date cash-payments review for unrecorded liabilities.

## 8. Suggested tests of controls

- [P-PUR-002] Reperform the three-way matching control
- [P-PUR-007] Inspect the supplier master change log and approvals
- [P-PUR-012] Inspect whether paid invoices are marked to prevent reprocessing

## 9. Suggested substantive analytical procedures

- [AP-PUR-401] Payables days vs payment terms trend
- [AP-PUR-402] Purchases vs inventory movement reasonableness
- [AP-PUR-403] Post-year-end payment scan for unrecorded liabilities

## 10. Suggested tests of details

- [P-PUR-001] Vouch purchase invoices to goods received notes and purchase orders
- [P-PUR-003] Inspect the unmatched-invoices exception report
- [P-PUR-004] Trace pre-year-end goods received notes to the purchase ledger
- [P-PUR-005] Test post-year-end purchase invoices for pre-year-end receipt
- [P-PUR-006] Inspect the year-end accrual for unmatched goods received
- [P-PUR-008] Vouch payments to newly added or changed suppliers
- [P-PUR-009] Analyse the supplier master for indicators of fictitious suppliers
- [P-PUR-010] Use data analysis to identify potential duplicate invoices
- [P-PUR-011] Vouch suspected duplicate invoices to invoice copies and payment records
- [P-PUR-013] Test purchase cut-off around the reporting date
- [P-PUR-014] Trace goods received notes to the purchase ledger for completeness
- [P-PUR-015] Analyse monthly purchase trends for cut-off anomalies

## 11. Sampling considerations

Vouching: sample purchases to GRNs and invoices. Completeness: select from GRNs/after-date payments back to the ledger (directional testing). Supplier reconciliations for all material suppliers.

## 12. Evidence to obtain

- [E-PUR-001] Supplier invoices
- [E-PUR-002] Goods received notes
- [E-PUR-003] Purchase orders and matching records
- [E-PUR-004] Goods received notes around year-end
- [E-PUR-005] Purchase ledger extracts after year-end
- [E-PUR-006] Year-end accrual schedules for unmatched GRNs
- [E-PUR-007] Supplier master change log
- [E-PUR-008] Approval records for supplier master changes
- [E-PUR-009] Supplier verification documents and payment records
- [E-PUR-010] Purchase ledger data extracts
- [E-PUR-011] Supplier invoice copies and payment records
- [E-PUR-012] Duplicate detection exception reports
- [E-PUR-013] Purchase invoices with posting and receipt dates
- [E-PUR-014] Period-end cut-off working papers
- [E-PUR-015] Monthly purchase reports and budgets

## 13. Expected documentation

For each procedure: objective, procedure performed, population and sample basis, evidence obtained (with references), results, exceptions and their resolution, and a conclusion linked to the assertion. Preparer and reviewer sign-off with dates. Cross-reference working papers so a reviewer can reperform the work.

## 14. Evaluation of exceptions

Unrecorded liabilities: require accrual, assess pervasiveness. Cut-off errors: extend testing around the period end. Supplier statement differences: resolve each.

## 15. Possible further procedures

Where exceptions indicate a systematic issue: extend the procedure, perform alternative procedures, involve specialists (valuers, tax, IT), or escalate to the engagement manager. Document the reasoning for the chosen response — procedure count alone proves nothing.

## 16. Completion considerations

After-date payments review; analytical review of expense ratios and payable days; accruals agreed to supporting evidence.

## 17. Conclusion requirements

# Audit programme: Property, plant and equipment

*Area: CYC-PPE — Property, plant and equipment | Illustrative programme (not a firm methodology) | 2026-10-23*

## 1. Engagement context and assumptions

Risks centre on existence and ownership of a dispersed asset base, correct capitalisation (repairs vs improvements), and depreciation reasonableness. Work-in-progress and self-constructed assets add measurement complexity; valuers may be involved.

Assumptions: the programme is adapted to the entity's size, systems, assessed risks and materiality. It does not replace professional judgement or the engagement partner's direction.

## 2. Objective

Obtain sufficient appropriate evidence over the existence, ownership, valuation and presentation of PPE.

## 3. Relevant financial statement areas

- CYC-PPE: Property, plant and equipment

## 4. Relevant assertions

- [BAL-EXI] Existence
- [BAL-VAL] Accuracy, valuation and allocation
- [DIS-COM] Completeness
- [TRN-ACC] Accuracy
- [TRN-CLS] Classification

## 5. Potential risks

- [R-PPE-001] **Inappropriate capitalisation of repairs and maintenance expenditure** — Revenue expenditure on repairs and maintenance may be capitalised as property, plant and equipment even though it does not meet the recognition criteria for an ...
- [R-PPE-002] **Incorrect depreciation charges and carrying amounts** — Depreciation may be understated or overstated, and the carrying amount of property, plant and equipment misstated, because the rates, methods or useful lives ap...
- [R-PPE-003] **Disposed assets remain recognised in the accounting records** — Assets that have been sold, scrapped, demolished or otherwise disposed of may continue to be recognised in the fixed asset register and the general ledger. The ...
- [R-PPE-004] **Unrecognised impairment losses** — Where indicators of impairment exist but are not identified or evaluated, impairment losses may not be recognised and the carrying amount of assets may exceed t...
- [R-PPE-005] **Replaced significant components not derecognised** — When a significant component of an asset is replaced, the carrying amount of the replaced part may remain in the asset's cost alongside the cost of the new part...

## 6. Relevant controls

- [C-PPE-001] Ensure only expenditure meeting the capitalisation criteria is recognised as property, plant and equipment.
- [C-PPE-002] Detect misclassification between repairs expense and capital additions.
- [C-PPE-003] Ensure depreciation reflects the expected pattern of consumption of future economic benefits.
- [C-PPE-004] Prevent unauthorised or undocumented changes to depreciation parameters.
- [C-PPE-005] Ensure every disposal is authorised and removed from the accounting records.
- [C-PPE-006] Detect assets that no longer exist but remain on the register.
- [C-PPE-007] Ensure impairment indicators are identified so that impairment testing is performed when required.
- [C-PPE-008] Provide timely warning of underperformance that may indicate impairment.
- [C-PPE-009] Ensure replaced significant parts are removed from the carrying amount.
- [C-PPE-010] Enable separate depreciation and derecognition of significant parts.

## 7. Preliminary planning considerations

Understand the capitalisation policy and approval limits for capex. Identify WIP, assets under construction, and any revaluations (valuer competence and objectivity). Plan physical verification coverage, including title-deed inspection for land/buildings.

## 8. Suggested tests of controls

- [P-PPE-001-002] Inspect the capitalisation policy and test approval controls
- [P-PPE-002-003] Test authorisation of changes to depreciation parameters

## 9. Suggested substantive analytical procedures

- [AP-PPE-601] Depreciation charge vs asset base reasonableness
- [AP-PPE-602] Capital expenditure vs budget and revenue growth
- [AP-PPE-603] Repairs and maintenance vs asset age trend

## 10. Suggested tests of details

- [P-PPE-001-001] Test the classification of repairs and maintenance expenditure
- [P-PPE-001-003] Perform analytical procedures over repairs and maintenance expense
- [P-PPE-002-001] Recalculate depreciation for a sample of assets
- [P-PPE-002-002] Evaluate the appropriateness of useful lives and depreciation methods
- [P-PPE-003-001] Physically verify a sample of assets from the register
- [P-PPE-003-002] Inspect disposal records and verify the accounting for disposals
- [P-PPE-003-003] Search for unrecorded disposals
- [P-PPE-004-001] Evaluate management's impairment indicator assessment
- [P-PPE-004-002] Perform analytical procedures to identify impairment indicators
- [P-PPE-004-003] Inspect impairment tests and challenge key assumptions
- [P-PPE-005-001] Inspect replacement work orders and verify derecognition of replaced parts
- [P-PPE-005-002] Test componentisation of significant assets
- [P-PPE-005-003] Observe significant replacement work

## 11. Sampling considerations

100% examination of material additions; sample disposals and depreciation recalculations. Physical verification on a rotational or risk-weighted basis for large populations.

## 12. Evidence to obtain

- [E-PPE-001] Capitalisation policy
- [E-PPE-002] Repairs and maintenance ledger and supporting invoices
- [E-PPE-003] Capital expenditure approval records
- [E-PPE-004] Fixed asset register
- [E-PPE-005] Auditor's depreciation recalculation
- [E-PPE-006] Management's useful-life review documentation
- [E-PPE-007] Asset disposal authorisation forms
- [E-PPE-008] Disposal proceeds records
- [E-PPE-009] Auditor's physical verification notes
- [E-PPE-010] Impairment indicator assessment
- [E-PPE-011] Management forecasts and budgets
- [E-PPE-012] External market or valuation data
- [E-PPE-013] Major maintenance and replacement work orders
- [E-PPE-014] Component register detail

## 13. Expected documentation

For each procedure: objective, procedure performed, population and sample basis, evidence obtained (with references), results, exceptions and their resolution, and a conclusion linked to the assertion. Preparer and reviewer sign-off with dates. Cross-reference working papers so a reviewer can reperform the work.

## 14. Evaluation of exceptions

Repairs capitalised: propose adjustment. Assets not in use without impairment review: challenge. Missing title deeds: document and consider implications.

## 15. Possible further procedures

Where exceptions indicate a systematic issue: extend the procedure, perform alternative procedures, involve specialists (valuers, tax, IT), or escalate to the engagement manager. Document the reasoning for the chosen response — procedure count alone proves nothing.

## 16. Completion considerations

Reconcile the fixed-asset register to the general ledger; analytical review of depreciation; review board minutes for unrecorded commitments.

## 17. Conclusion requirements

Conclude per assertion whether sufficient appropriate evidence was obtained. Unresolved exceptions are accumulated as misstatements and evaluated for materiality, individually and in aggregate. The conclusion must stand without the programme — a reviewer should reach the same conclusion from the working papers alone.

# Audit programme: Payroll and employee benefits

*Area: CYC-PAY — Payroll | Illustrative programme (not a firm methodology) | 2026-10-23*

## 1. Engagement context and assumptions

Payroll risk is occurrence (ghost employees, inflated hours) and completeness of accruals and payroll-tax liabilities. Strong IT-dependent controls often allow a controls-reliance approach, but master-file changes need scrutiny.

Assumptions: the programme is adapted to the entity's size, systems, assessed risks and materiality. It does not replace professional judgement or the engagement partner's direction.

## 2. Objective

Obtain sufficient appropriate evidence over the occurrence, completeness and accuracy of payroll costs and related liabilities.

## 3. Relevant financial statement areas

- CYC-PAY: Payroll

## 4. Relevant assertions

- [BAL-EXI] Existence
- [BAL-VAL] Accuracy, valuation and allocation
- [TRN-ACC] Accuracy
- [TRN-OCC] Occurrence

## 5. Potential risks

- [R-PAY-001] **Payments to ghost or terminated employees** — Wages, allowances or termination-related payments continue to be processed for individuals who have left employment, diverting funds and overstating payroll cos...
- [R-PAY-002] **Fictitious employees created or pay details manipulated** — An individual with combined custody of employee records and payments could create fictitious employees, inflate pay rates, alter bank details, or process duplic...
- [R-PAY-003] **Inflated or fictitious overtime payments** — Employees may claim overtime not worked, or record excessive hours, and the amounts are paid without detection, overstating payroll costs....
- [R-PAY-004] **Payroll expense and deductions misstated through calculation errors** — Systematic or isolated errors in pay rates, tax calculations or deductions cause wages, tax liabilities and related balances to be misstated....

## 6. Relevant controls

- [C-PAY-001] Ensure terminated employees are removed promptly so no further payments are processed.
- [C-PAY-002] Detect ghost or terminated employees remaining on the payroll.
- [C-PAY-003] Prevent unauthorised or fictitious changes to employee master data.
- [C-PAY-004] Prevent one person from both creating a payee and paying them.
- [C-PAY-005] Ensure only genuine, necessary overtime is paid.
- [C-PAY-006] Detect excessive or anomalous overtime claims.
- [C-PAY-007] Ensure payroll is calculated from correct, current rates and parameters.
- [C-PAY-008] Detect calculation errors and ensure payroll agrees with the accounting records.

## 7. Preliminary planning considerations

Understand the payroll system, who can amend the master file, and how starters/leavers are processed. Reconcile headcount: payroll vs HR records. Identify related payroll taxes and their filing deadlines.

## 8. Suggested tests of controls

- [P-PAY-004] Inspect the leaver-to-payroll process
- [P-PAY-005] Inspect payroll system access rights
- [P-PAY-012] Test the overtime approval control

## 9. Suggested substantive analytical procedures

- [AP-PAY-501] Payroll cost per head vs prior year and budget
- [AP-PAY-502] Overtime as a percentage of payroll trend
- [AP-PAY-503] Headcount per payroll vs HR records

## 10. Suggested tests of details

- [P-PAY-001] Analyse payroll cost trends by department and headcount
- [P-PAY-002] Trace leavers to removal from the payroll master
- [P-PAY-003] Vouch a sample of payees to current employment evidence
- [P-PAY-006] Vouch master changes to independent approval
- [P-PAY-007] Reperform the payroll calculation for a sample of employees
- [P-PAY-008] Analyse new starters and bank detail changes
- [P-PAY-009] Vouch overtime payments to approved timesheets
- [P-PAY-010] Analyse overtime trends and exceptions
- [P-PAY-011] Recalculate overtime pay
- [P-PAY-013] Recalculate net pay for a sample of employees
- [P-PAY-014] Agree pay rates to authorised sources
- [P-PAY-015] Reconcile payroll to the general ledger and investigate differences
- [P-PAY-016] Analytical review of payroll cost per head

## 11. Sampling considerations

Sample payroll runs across the year; reperform net-pay calculations for the sample. Test ALL master-file amendments in the period if the population is small.

## 12. Evidence to obtain

- [E-PAY-001] Payroll register (payroll summary)
- [E-PAY-002] HR leavers list (termination register)
- [E-PAY-003] Employment records (HR files)
- [E-PAY-004] Payroll master change audit trail
- [E-PAY-005] User access rights report
- [E-PAY-006] Approved payroll change requests
- [E-PAY-007] Overtime claim forms / timesheets
- [E-PAY-008] Attendance / production records
- [E-PAY-009] Overtime exception report
- [E-PAY-010] Authorised pay rates and statutory tables
- [E-PAY-011] General ledger payroll accounts

## 13. Expected documentation

For each procedure: objective, procedure performed, population and sample basis, evidence obtained (with references), results, exceptions and their resolution, and a conclusion linked to the assertion. Preparer and reviewer sign-off with dates. Cross-reference working papers so a reviewer can reperform the work.

## 14. Evaluation of exceptions

Ghost employees or unverified starters: investigate fully — potential fraud indicator. Payroll-tax under-accruals: quantify and accumulate.

## 15. Possible further procedures

Where exceptions indicate a systematic issue: extend the procedure, perform alternative procedures, involve specialists (valuers, tax, IT), or escalate to the engagement manager. Document the reasoning for the chosen response — procedure count alone proves nothing.

## 16. Completion considerations

Analytical review of payroll cost ratios and headcount trends; subsequent payroll payments agreed; tax filings agreed to the ledger.

## 17. Conclusion requirements

Conclude per assertion whether sufficient appropriate evidence was obtained. Unresolved exceptions are accumulated as misstatements and evaluated for materiality, individually and in aggregate. The conclusion must stand without the programme — a reviewer should reach the same conclusion from the working papers alone.

- Companies Act, 2017 ss.246–253 (auditor provisions) [KR-CA2017-246 … KR-CA2017-253]
